```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(cdzoo)
has_pcalg <- requireNamespace("pcalg", quietly = TRUE)
set.seed(1)
```

Most discovery tools need a row-level data matrix. A great deal of real
association data, though, arrives already aggregated -- a published correlation
matrix, a privacy-preserving summary, or pairwise co-occurrence counts -- with
no rows to hand. `cdzoo` treats a sufficient statistic as a first-class input:
you can discover from it directly, or let the recommender route it.

## Counts to a correlation matrix

Co-occurrence data is often published as pairwise two-by-two tables: for each
pair of binary variables, the counts of both present, one present, or neither.
`cd_correlation_from_counts()` assembles a positive-definite correlation matrix
from those counts, repairing it to the nearest valid correlation matrix when the
pairwise assembly is not itself positive-definite:

```{r counts}
pairs <- data.frame(
  var_i = c("a", "a", "b"),
  var_j = c("b", "c", "c"),
  n11 = c(900, 110, 105),
  n10 = c(100, 890, 895),
  n01 = c(100, 90, 95),
  n00 = c(8900, 8910, 8905))
C <- cd_correlation_from_counts(pairs, type = "phi")
round(C, 2)
attr(C, "repair")[c("eig_min_raw", "eig_min", "distortion")]
```

## Discovery from the statistic

`cd_discover_suffstat()` runs constraint-based discovery directly on the matrix
and its sample size. `method = "ggm"` needs no back-end and returns the
partial-correlation skeleton; `"pc"` and `"fci"` add orientation through
`pcalg`:

```{r discover}
res <- cd_discover_suffstat(C, n = 10000, method = "ggm")
cd_edges(res)
```

At population sample sizes a significance-based test rejects independence for
almost every pair, so the graph saturates. The magnitude test prunes by effect
size instead, which is the right behaviour when `n` is very large:

```{r magnitude, eval = has_pcalg}
sim <- cd_scenario("linear_gaussian", seed = 1)
big <- stats::cor(sim$data)
gauss <- cd_discover_suffstat(big, n = 5e6, method = "pc", test = "gauss")
magnitude <- cd_discover_suffstat(big, n = 5e6, method = "pc", test = "magnitude")
c(gauss = nrow(cd_edges(gauss)), magnitude = nrow(cd_edges(magnitude)))
```

## Letting the recommender route it

Wrapping the statistic as `cd_suffstat()` lets `cd_auto()` recommend a method.
A correlation matrix carries only the latent-structure hint, so the
recommendation states plainly which diagnostics an aggregated input cannot
support:

```{r auto, eval = has_pcalg}
ss <- cd_suffstat(big, n = nrow(sim$data))
rec <- cd_auto(ss)
cd_explain(rec)
```

## Passing the result on

A recovered graph carries its provenance into the federation manifest exactly as
a data-driven result does, so an aggregated-input discovery is verifiable
downstream:

```{r manifest, eval = has_pcalg}
m <- as_orchestra_manifest(rec, seed = 1L)
m@inferential_target
verify_manifest(m)$ok
```

The whole path -- counts to a correlation matrix, discovery from the statistic,
a routed recommendation, and a verifiable manifest -- runs without ever holding
a row-level data set.
